Definition: from G2596 and G3007; to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining:--forsake, leave, reserve.
BiblicalUsage: To leave behind is what a man does to father and mother when he cleaves to his wife, what Moses did when he forsook Egypt not fearing the wrath of the king, and what God did not do when He reserved seven thousand men who had not bowed to Baal. The word holds both the leaving and the keeping: some things are left so better things can be kept, and some are kept because God never leaves them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe leaving is the price of cleaving, whether to a wife or to the God who calls me out. I hold that God always keeps a remnant for Himself, and I want to be among those He keeps.
